activity_context.topic_title: Cumulative Distribution Functions for Discrete Random Variables

examples.knowledge_point: Computing a Probability Over an Interval Containing a Greater Than Symbol
examples.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(X \gt 2).$

| $x$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ | $5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.6$ | $0.8$ | $0.9$ | $1.0$ |
examples.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x) = P(X \leq x).
$$

To solve the given problem, we can use the rule

$$
P(X > a) = 1 - P(X\leq a) = 1-F(a).
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & =1-F(2) \\  & =1-0.6 \\  & =0.4.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Given that the discrete random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function $F(x)$ shown in the table below, compute $P(-1.5<X\le 0.5).$

| $x$ | $-1.5$ | $-1$ | $-0.5$ | $0$ | $0.5$ | $1$ | $1.5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $F(x)$ | $\frac{1}{16}$ | $\frac{3}{16}$ | $\frac{5}{16}$ | $\frac{1}{2}$ | $\frac{9}{16}$ | $\frac{13}{16}$ | $1$ |
feedback.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a discrete random variable $X$ is a function $F(x)$ such that

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x).
$$

To compute the probability of a random variable $X$ over an interval, we can use the rule

$$
P(a<X\le b)=F(b)-F(a).
$$

Here, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-1.5<X\le 0.5) & =F(0.5)-F(-1.5) \\  & =\frac{9}{16}-\frac{1}{16} \\  & =\frac{8}{16} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
